_doc: ONE PAGE FOR THE PRIVILEGED CHANNEL. #1682 P3 the ADB owner is the Cloud C3 Webserver app: the ADB Shell page (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools AdbShellPage, hosted by the webserver's AdbOwnerSide) is the only place that PAIRS, CONNECTS, DISCONNECTS, starts or stops the local server, asks Shizuku for permission, switches the channel mode or opens the Wireless-debugging settings on the person's behalf. Every other screen shows a compact status chip that opens it (AdbShellLink.open / AdbShellChip / StoreBar.channelButton). Read by aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-adb-shell-one-place.sh, which fails when a first-party source file outside `allow` contains one of the `controls`, when an app that links the lib does not expose the page (`hosts`), or when the page grows a minimum height.

allow._doc: Every entry says why it is not a second control surface. A file listed here that no longer contains any control is STALE and fails: the list only shrinks. `dirs` are prefixes (the lib is the implementation).

dirs.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shizuku-adb-de: the implementation of the channel and its page

files.aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/java/com/: #1682 P3 the SuperApp's Wireless debugging switch (read, write by WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS or through the owner's broker) and the chip link to the phone's own Developer-options switch (openSettings); no pairing, no channel class
files.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/adb-shell-core: the loopback HTTP debug API (/api/adb/pair, /connect, ...) driven by curl; it is not a screen
background keeper that re-arms adb_wifi_enabled and raises one fleet alert whose deep link is the system screen only the person can use
files.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/wifi/src/main/: #1263 WiFi page: one button opens Developer options so the person can switch Wi-Fi scan throttling off; no pairing, connecting, server or adb state
files.ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/adb-shell-core: the ADB Shell page's own Status tab (AdbShellFragment, tab adb-status): its Mode selector is the page's mode switch, not a second surface
the verbs of that same Status tab (embedded adb Init / Reset, the Shizuku authorize prompt, Auto-fix); reached only from the ADB Shell page
files.aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/java/com/: Launcher > Controls system-switch tile for the Wireless debugging setting itself, beside Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; no pairing, connecting or server

hosts._doc: Every app whose gradle links the lib must expose the page, and must say what it needs the channel for (build.json::privileged_channel.needs). `has` is a string that must appear in `file`. #1682 P3: the ADB owner is the Cloud C3 Webserver app (ac_cloud-c3-webserver, AdbOwnerSide hosts AdbShellBrokerPage); Cloud Store, Cloud Account, the SuperApp and the terminals reach the shell through the owner's broker (libs:shell-client) and open the owner's page through AdbShellLink.open. `consumers` is what gradle must show linking the lib today (the SuperApp until its client build drops it; the guard fails when the list and gradle differ, so the cut-over cannot pass unnoticed). The ADB owner's own host entry is `owner_host` (it declares no privileged_channel.needs block yet; test-adb-page-owner-only.sh holds that it hosts the page).

owner_page._doc: #1682 THE ONE ADB PAGE IS THE OWNER'S (Cloud C3 Webserver). No first-party source outside the owner side may open the SuperApp's own ADB page: the in-app route (section config, page adb-shell / adb-status), the lib's AdbShellActivity of the superapp package. Every chip calls AdbShellLink.open. Read by ac_cloud-store/test/test-adb-page-owner-only.sh. `offenders` is a SHRINKING RATCHET, never an allow-forever: each entry is a file that still opens the SuperApp's page today and names the ticket step that removes it; a file that no longer matches is STALE and fails (delete the entry), a file not listed fails. The list only shrinks; it is empty when the SuperApp and Account commits land. ShellClient.openArmPage is NOT forbidden: its explicit intent targets ShellWire.BROKER_PKG, which must equal the owner app's application id (checked), so it is the client-safe door to the owner's page.

owner_side._doc: The only places allowed to name those (prefixes / files): the webserver app, the AdbShellLink opener, the shell-client lib that declares the intents, and the lib that implements the page.

offenders.aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/java/com/: #1682 the network popup's ADB row is Target.InApp config/adb-shell; the SuperApp agent retargets it to the owner
#1682 the SuperApp's AdbShellLink.hostOpener opens its own config/adb-shell route; removed with the SuperApp's own page

store_must_use._doc: Store code that opens the ADB page does it through the client door to the owner's page (or AdbShellLink.open where the owner lib is linked), nothing else.

owner_host._doc: #1682 P3 the ADB owner: the Cloud C3 Webserver app hosts THE one ADB Shell page (AdbShellBrokerPage inside its AdbOwnerSide). Held by test-adb-page-owner-only.sh (O4).
